safety_lead_time.comparison_action: Reduce SAP safety lead time from 2.5 to 1.67 days

narrative: Material PL2__M63EDC15 shows erratic but consistently active demand (CV=0.42, 97.8% non-zero days) with a mean of 4,376 units/day and unstable lead times (CV=0.81, mean=1.13 days). The current SAP policy of zero safety stock and MOQ=55 is severely misaligned with actual demand patterns, generating thousands of micro-orders annually. An (r,Q) continuous-review policy with EOQ-derived order quantity of 12,089 units and safety stock of 7,308 units achieves 95% service level while reducing total annual costs by over 98%.
warnings: SAP safety stock is 0 — no buffer against lead-time variability; stockout risk is high under current policy.

research_insights.selection_rationale: Demand is erratic but near-continuous (97.8% non-zero), making a continuous-review (r,Q) model appropriate. EOQ minimises total ordering and holding costs given the high daily volume; safety stock sized via the sigma-LTD formula accounts for both demand and lead-time variability.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Order quantity (12,089) plus safety stock (7,308) = 19,397 units, well within the 36,800-unit storage capacity. No capacity binding.
